data.title: Walker & Dunlop Arranges $270 Million Refinancing for Nasser Freres’ The Greyson in Jersey City
data.description:
Walker & Dunlop, Inc. announced today that it has arranged $270,000,000 in refinancing for The Greyson, a 28-story, 622-unit, Class A mixed-use residential tower developed by Nasser Freres in the heart of Jersey City's Journal Square neighborhood. The financing marks a significant milestone for the development, supporting its transition from construction to stabilized operations and positioning the property for long-term success.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118022862/en/

The Greyson. Photo credits: Nasser Freres

Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory served as exclusive advisor to Nasser Freres, arranging a floating-rate, interest-only bridge loan from affiliates of Apollo. The transaction was arranged by Keith Kurland, Aaron Appel, Adam Schwartz, Jonathan Schwartz, Jordan Casella, Christopher de Raet, and Jack Krentzman.

"Journal Square has undergone a remarkable transformation, and The Greyson exemplifies the caliber of development attracting investment to the neighborhood,” said Kurland, senior managing director of Capital Markets and co-head of Institutional Advisory at Walker & Dunlop. "With its exceptional location, extensive amenities, and proximity to Manhattan, the property is well-positioned to capitalize on the area’s continued growth. We’re pleased to have worked with Nasser Freres and Apollo to execute this transaction.”

Located at 25 Cottage Street, The Greyson encompasses 424,328 rentable square feet, including 389,328 square feet of residential and 35,000 square feet of commercial space. The property features a collection of studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences with unobstructed views of the Jersey City skyline. Designed to deliver an elevated residential experience, The Greyson offers an extensive suite of amenities, including an art gallery, children's playroom, screening room, gaming lounge, virtual reality and sports room, coffee bar, fitness center, speakeasy, and private event space. Ground-floor retail space leased to a wine bar further enhances the property’s appeal while contributing to Journal Square’s growing dining and entertainment scene.

"From the outset, our vision for The Greyson was to create something truly distinctive, a property that would help shape the next chapter of residential living in Journal Square while contributing meaningfully to the neighborhood’s continued transformation,” said Michael Sokoloff, partner at Nasser Freres. "We’ve been intentional about every aspect of this development, from its architecture and design to the amenities and experiences we’re bringing to residents. We’re incredibly proud of what we’ve built and believe The Greyson will set a new standard for the neighborhood for years to come. This refinancing marks an exciting next chapter as we shift our focus to the property’s long-term success and we appreciate Walker & Dunlop’s advisory.”

Situated along the newly opened Homestead commercial corridor, the property is less than a five-minute walk from the Journal Square Transportation Center, offering direct PATH access to Lower and Midtown Manhattan in approximately 10 and 20 minutes, respectively. Journal Square has emerged as one of the New York metropolitan area's fastest-growing rental submarkets, driven by demand for transit-oriented housing and rental rates that remain comparatively affordable to those along the Jersey City Waterfront and in Manhattan.

In the first half of 2026, Walker & Dunlop’s Capital Markets team sourced over $13.9 billion from non-Agency capital providers, including nearly $9.6 billion for multifamily properties. This vast experience has made them a top advisor on all asset classes for many of the industry’s top developers, owners, and operators. To learn more about Walker & Dunlop’s broad financing options, visit our website.

About Walker & Dunlop

Walker & Dunlop () is one of the largest commercial real estate finance and advisory services firms in the United States and internationally. Our ideas and capital create communities where people live, work, shop, and play. Our innovative people, breadth of our brand, and our technological capabilities make us one of the most insightful and client-focused firms in the commercial real estate industry.

data.title: First Graphene Expands Composites Development into China with UNITEX
data.description:
Highlights

  • Joint Development and Commercialisation Agreement signed with UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd., part of UNITEX Group, a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications, combining development and manufacturing capabilities in China with an established customer network spanning more than 100 countries.
  • Initial focus on graphene enhanced carbon fibre prepreg, with plans to expand into thermoplastics, resin concentrates, coatings and elastomers.
  • Agreement combines First Graphene's formulation and dispersion expertise with UNITEX's manufacturing and innovation capabilities, and established international supply network.
  • Provides First Graphene with a pathway into China's composites manufacturing and innovation sector and access to wider international markets, helping to accelerate the development, scale-up and global commercialisation of graphene-enhanced materials across a broad range of applications.

Sydney, Australia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - First Graphene Limited  (FSE: M11) (OTCQB: FGPHF) ("First Graphene" or "the Company") is pleased to announce it has entered into a Joint Development and Commercialisation Agreement ("the Agreement") with UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd. ("UNITEX"), establishing a strategic collaboration to develop and commercialise graphene enhanced carbon fibre composites and other advanced materials.

The Agreement represents a further step in First Graphene's strategy to commercialise its graphene technologies through strategic development and manufacturing partnerships. The collaboration draws on UNITEX's material development, engineering and manufacturing capabilities in China, providing First Graphene with a pathway into China's significant composites manufacturing sector and the international markets it supplies.

Headquartered in Ningbo, China's Zhejiang province, UNITEX is a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications. Built on its manufacturing capabilities in China, the group combines material development, application engineering and industrial supply chain integration to translate material technologies into commercially viable products and solutions.

With an established customer network spanning more than 100 countries, UNITEX serves industries including automotive, aerospace, semiconductors, energy, marine, construction and sporting goods.

Its capabilities extend from customised material development and engineering support to industrial-scale manufacturing and global supply, providing a foundation for the international commercialisation of jointly developed materials.

The collaboration will combine First Graphene's expertise in graphene selection, formulation and dispersion with UNITEX's materials engineering, manufacturing infrastructure and established supply chain capabilities.

Development and commercialisation program

The initial development program will focus on graphene enhanced carbon fibre prepreg, building on First Graphene's internal research and development activities, which demonstrated improvements in strength and barrier properties through incorporation of graphene into carbon fibre composites.

Where the results justify further development, the parties intend to progress successful formulations through customer validation, manufacturing scale-up and commercialisation, subject to the agreement of applicable commercial terms. The Agreement term is for three years and is cancellable by either party with three months notice.

Beyond carbon fibre prepreg, the collaboration is expected to explore opportunities across thermoplastics, resin concentrates, coatings, elastomers and other advanced materials, broadening the potential applications and commercial reach of First Graphene's graphene technologies.

The Agreement provides First Graphene with an opportunity to leverage UNITEX's material development, engineering and manufacturing capabilities, together with its established international customer network, to accelerate the development and industrialisation of graphene enhanced materials and bring commercially viable products to global markets.

First Graphene Managing Director and CEO, Michael Bell, said:

"Carbon fibre and advanced composites represent an increasingly important growth opportunity for First Graphene, as manufacturers seek innovative ways to improve material performance and deliver greater value to customers.

Our internal development work has demonstrated the potential of graphene to enhance the strength and barrier properties of carbon fibre composites. The next step is translating technical advances into commercially scalable products through partnerships with established manufacturers.

UNITEX brings extensive expertise in materials development, engineering and manufacturing, alongside an established international customer network. This collaboration provides FGR with a strategic pathway into China's composites manufacturing sector and expand its commercial reach across global markets.

Importantly, the opportunity extends well beyond carbon fibre. By combining our respective technical and manufacturing capabilities, we see significant potential to develop graphene-enhanced thermoplastics, coatings and other advanced materials across industrial applications.

This agreement is another important step in our strategy to move graphene innovation from development into commercial markets and expand First Graphene's international presence."

About UNITEX

UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd., established in 2017 and headquartered in Ningbo, China, is part of UNITEX Group, a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications. Built on its manufacturing capabilities in China and the integration of China's comprehensive industrial supply chain, UNITEX brings together material development, application engineering and industrialisation to deliver customised solutions for global customers. The group serves customers in more than 100 countries, supporting a broad range of industries from material development through to commercial production and international supply.

-Ends-

This announcement has been approved by the Chairman.

For further information please contact:

  • Investors Michael Bell Managing Director and CEO First Graphene Limited michael.bell@firstgraphene.net +61 1300 660 448 
  • Media Josh Nyman General Manager SPOKE. josh@hellospoke.com.au +61 413 243 440

About First Graphene Ltd

First Graphene Limited is focused on the development of advanced materials to help industry improve. The Company is a leading supplier of graphitic materials and product formulations with a specific commercial focus on large, high-growth global markets including cement and concrete; composites and plastics; coatings, adhesives, sealants and elastomers (CASE); and energy storage applications.

One of the key outcomes these advanced materials offer is the reduction of carbon dioxide emissions, whether directly through a reduction in output of these harmful greenhouse gases or lower energy usage requirements in manufacturing, or indirectly due to enhanced performance characteristics and extending the usable life of products.

First Graphene has a robust manufacturing platform based on captive and abundant supply of high-purity raw materials, and readily scalable technologies to meet growing market demand. As well as being the world's leading supplier of its own high performance PureGRAPH® graphene product range, the Company works with multiple industry partners around the world as a supplier of graphitic materials and partner to research, develop, test and facilitate the commercial marketing of a wide range of sector-specific chemical solutions.

First Graphene Ltd is publicly listed in Australia and has a primary manufacturing base in Henderson, near Perth, WA. The Company is incorporated in the UK as First Graphene (UK) Ltd where it has a strong R&D capability.

data.title: Australian employment falls sharply in October, jobless rate hits 5-year high
data.description:
Australian employment fell for a second straight month in October and the jobless rate climbed to a five-year high, a surprisingly soft result that bolstered the case that interest rates have likely reached their peak.

Markets are now certain that the Reserve Bank of Australia is done raising interest rates after five rate hikes this year took the cash rate to an 18-year high of 4.85%. Around 38 basis points of easing is priced in by the end of next year, up sharply from 23 bps before the data. (0#AUDIRPR)

The Australian dollar (AUD=3) was down 0.3% to a 10-month low of $0.6698, while three-year government bond futures (YTTc1) rallied 11 ticks to 95.39, the highest since late August.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics said employment fell by 43,500 in October from September, when it dropped a revised 36,400. Analysts had forecast a rise of around 25,000.

The jobless rate climbed to 4.9%, the highest since October 2021, from 4.7% a month ago. The participation rate dipped to 66.6%, while hours worked fell 0.2%.

The weak data contrasted with a surprise jump in wages that pointed to some persistent inflationary pressures in the economy. The RBA had flagged wage growth as a factor in its decision to raise rates earlier this month, having judged the labour market was tighter than it had previously thought.

However, anecdotal evidence of a broader rise in layoffs is building and the RBA board members who voted against a hike this month had flagged the risk the economy was facing a sharper-than-expected downturn.

Retailer David Jones will cut about 1,500 jobs after its collapse into administration, a union said on Wednesday, joining a string of job losses at Australian firms as the economy slows.

data.title: Japanese bond yields fall on safe-haven demand, lower oil
data.description:
By Satoshi Sugiyama

Japanese government bond (JGB) yields fell on Thursday as investors sought safe-haven assets amid jitters in equity markets and stabilized oil prices eased inflation fears.

Here are a few details:

  • The benchmark 10-year JGB yield (JP10YTN=JBTC) fell 1.5 basis points (bps) to 2.855%. Yields move inversely to bond prices

  • The 20-year JGB yield (JP20YTN=JBTC) slid 2.5bps to 3.755%. The 30-year yield (JP30YTN=JBTC) sank 2.5bps to 4.030%. The 5-year yield (JP5YTN=JBTC) fell 1bp to 2.245%

  • Longer-dated US bond yields eased overnight as oil prices fell and after last week’s sharp run-up. Oil prices settled down more than 1% on Wednesday after US crude and fuel inventories posted larger-than-expected rises, adding to expectations of a supply surplus

  • "Buying is likely to take the lead, supported by lower crude oil prices and higher US Treasuries, but the market is expected to struggle to extend gains as domestic JGB supply-demand conditions and expectations for further BOJ rate hikes weigh," said Takayuki Miyajima, senior economist at Sony Financial Group, in a note

  • On Wednesday, Japan's 20-year government bond yield rose after an auction for bonds with the same maturity drew weak demand, even though yields on most maturities fell

  • Analysts express caution over the supply-and-demand outlook for superlong maturities

  • "Probably because pension funds have been key investors in superlong JGBs, the pullback in demand during the equity market decline is seen as the biggest negative factor," said Ataru Okumura, chief rates strategist at SMBC Nikko Securities, in a note. "If share prices fail to rebound, concerns are likely to persist over upcoming superlong JGB auctions as well"

data.title: Japan Data Preview: Hotter Inflation Expected in October CPI Report
data.description:
Consensus outlook for Mace News

Friday, Nov 20, 2026

0830 JST (2330 GMT/1830 EST Thursday, Nov 19) The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications releases October CPI.

Mace News median: total CPI +2.6% y/y (range: +2.3% to +2.8%) vs. Sept +2.1%; core CPI (ex-fresh food) +2.4% y/y (range: +2.3% to +2.6%) vs. Sept +2.1%; core-core CPI (ex-fresh food, energy) +2.3% y/y (range: +2.3% to +2.7%) vs. Sept +2.4%

TOKYO (MaceNews) - Japan’s consumer inflation is expected to accelerate in two of the three major readings in October as the uptrend in prices becomes clearer and spreads across a wider range of goods and services, following a similar trend seen in the country’s capital.

After all three key measures of the nationwide consumer price index (CPI) rose above the Bank of Japan’s 2% inflation target in September for the first time in six months, the October readings are expected to show further gains, with two reaching their highest levels in 2026.

Higher energy, metal and other raw material costs, as well as food and beverage prices, are contributing to the increase, with the persistent weakness of the yen further pushing up import costs.

This trend was already evident in the Tokyo CPI, a leading indicator of the nationwide trend. The October reading showed broad-based inflation gains across various items, including food, rent, household consumables, auto insurance, train fares, education and hotel fees.

The core index, which excludes fresh food, is expected to rise 2.4%, compared with 2.1% in September. This would be the highest reading since December 2025, when it rose by the same amount.

The total CPI is projected to rise to 2.6% in October from 2.1% in September, marking its highest level since November 2025, when it increased 2.9%.

Meanwhile, the core-core figure, which excludes fresh food and energy, is expected to decelerate to a 2.3% year-on-year rise in October, compared with a 2.4% increase in the previous month.

data.title: Australia's Jobless Rate Rises to Highest Level Since 2021
data.description:
By James Glynn

SYDNEY--Australia's unemployment rate jumped in October to its highest level since late 2021, highlighting fears that the economy is slowing rapidly due to weak confidence and five interest-rate increases since the start of the year.

Unemployment hit 4.9% in October, up from 4.7% in September, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said Thursday.

The economy lost 43,500 jobs in the month, with part-time employment falling by 40,600.

Higher unemployment will argue strongly for the Reserve Bank of Australia to keep interest rates on hold from here, albeit data on Wednesday showed wages grew at their fastest pace since 2023 in the third quarter.

RBA Gov. Michele Bullock also affirmed this week her view that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside.

Inflation data for October will be released next week, with economists warning that there is a high risk that it will once again surprise on the high side of estimates.

Still, the impact of interest-rate increases this year is becoming increasingly obvious, with lending for new homes collapsing and house prices heading toward record losses.

The RBA has talked about the difficult policy task before, highlighting that elevated inflation remains its main priority.

The bank recently forecast that inflation will remain above target until mid-2028, amid concerns inflation expectations are becoming embedded.

The employment-to-population ratio fell 0.3 percentage point to 63.3%, and the participation rate fell 0.2 percentage point to 66.6%

The number of hours worked fell 0.2% in October, while the underemployment rate fell 0.1 percentage point to 6.2%

-Write to James Glynn at james.glynn@wsj.com

data.title: The key S&P 500 level Wall Street is watching
data.description:
The S&P broke through a key support level Tuesday, a bad sign for what's to come.

The benchmark ended Tuesday's session at 7,340.53, just under its 200-day moving average of 7,346.64. That marked its first close below the 200-day since April 7. From a technical standpoint, this doesn't bode well for a rebound.

"With SPX once again testing the top of the 7250-7350 support zone, we suspect it's one too many tests," Jonathan Krinsky, chief market technician at BTIG, in a note.

Stocks were flat Wednesday with the S&P 500 around 7,342 shortly after 10 am.

Through Tuesday's close, the S&P 500 was down 3.2% over the past month, weighed by uncertainty around the artificial intelligence trade and a scandal that engulfed Nvidia that led to Jensen Huang's departure as CEO.

JPMorgan's market intelligence team is tactically bullish stocks.

"While the AI trade has given the market more to think about, demand is insatiable but the pace of the build out may be slower, which is not necessarily a bad thing as the commercial adoption rate and productivity gains increase," it said in a note this week.

TS Lombard strategist Dario Perkins also pointed to four reasons why the AI trade can continue:

  • "Hyperscalers are yet to downgrade their strong capex plans;
  • compute demand remains impressively solid, as we can see from GPU rental prices;
  • the Fed has only just started its new policy tightening cycle;
  • there is always a market correction – followed by a prompt rebound – ahead of the ultimate crash."

But BTIG's Krinsky thinks the outlook for the market will get worse before it improves.

"We continue to see too many views that we need a bounce or we are oversold. That might have been the case on November 5th, but the market used up its oversold conditions and is now in a much weaker spot as it once again tests the key support zone of for the fifth time since early June."

With the S&P 500 breaking below its 200-day, its next stop might be the 7,000-7,100 zone, Krinsky added.

data.title: Jump in Australia's Jobless Rate Likely to Kill off Further Hikes — Market Talk
data.description: Australia's unemployment rose to its highest level since 2021 in October, sharply eroding the case for a further rise in interest rates. Achieving the RBA's dual mandate of full employment and sustained low inflation is getting more complex as the job market weakens and inflation stays elevated. Still, the central bank will be much more cautious going forward given indications that hiring has slowed. The RBA had been arguing that the job market remains tight. The October employment data will likely change that view, with policy makers likely to wait to see the impact of rate hikes already delivered. (james.glynn@wsj.com; Twitter @JamesGlynnWSJ)

data.title: Everforth, Inc. Announces Withdrawal of Proposed Senior Notes Offering
data.description:
Everforth, Inc. () (“Everforth”) announced today that it has withdrawn its previously proposed offering of $500 million in aggregate principal amount of senior notes due 2031 as a result of market conditions.

The proposed transaction was opportunistic to refinance the Company’s existing 4.625% senior notes well in advance of their May 2028 maturity. While Everforth had meaningful investor interest, the Company made the strategic decision to withdraw the offering as the terms do not reflect the strength of its business.

Everforth’s strong free cash flow and liquidity position provide the Company with significant financial flexibility. Everforth remains committed to using its free cash flow to reduce debt and further strengthen the balance sheet. The Company will continue to evaluate a range of financing alternatives to address the 2028 maturity.

data.title: Here's what every major Wall Street analyst is saying about Nvidia after its earnings report
data.description:
Nvidia's latest earnings report inspired confidence among investors on Wall Street, even after the stock's recent plunge due to a spy scandal involving its long-time CEO and top dealmaker, Jensen Huang.

The chipmaker posted fiscal third-quarter results that beat the Street. The company also lifted its fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecast to 75% from 70%, despite China being excluded from its data center compute revenue outlook. It also said it expects to bring in $130 billion in revenue for the current quarter, more than the LSEG consensus of $125.1 billion.

Shares of Nvidia jumped following the report, last up 3%.

Those gains come on the heels of a particularly volatile period for Nvidia. Former CEO Jensen Huang announced his resignation from the company last week after reports of several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.

Nvidia has lost roughly 24% this month.

Huang was central to securing many of Nvidia's landmark artificial intelligence-related deals, and he navigated the chipmaker through several industry shifts over the course of his more than 30-year tenure at the company.

Several Wall Street analysts say the overhang on Nvidia's shares created by the scandal and the subsequent departure of its prolific leader should soon clear up, particularly following the firm's latest earnings report and strong forward-looking commentary.

"Although significant uncertainty remains on several fronts, we believe management's commentary should bolster investor confidence in the fundamental outlook for both Nvidia's business and the broader AI ecosystem across a number of dimensions," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said Tuesday in a note to clients.

Schneider has a buy rating on Nvidia. He also has a $220 price target on shares, which is nearly 42% above the price at which Nvidia last closed.

Here's what else the Street is saying about Nvidia.

Bank of America: Buy rating, $280 price target

"While it may be premature to sound the all-clear, NVDA's earnings call was very reassuring as the company, under Interim CEO Kress, appears to be pulling together strongly in defiance of the skeptics."

Morgan Stanley: Overweight, $260

The bank trimmed its price target from $267.

"The strength we continue to see in the business is not a surprise, but the willingness to provide the level of forward-looking commentary we heard on the call was a significant positive. We remain in the early stages of a new product cycle seeing significant demand, that much is known after last quarter's FY28 guidance and through cloud earnings. But given the uncertainty with respect to Commerce Department actions (link), reports of DOJ and SEC investigations (link, link), as well as Nvidia's own internal investigation related to the CEO transition, we considered it a strong possibility Nvidia would not provide any updates to its prior FY28 guidance."

Bernstein: Market perform, $200

"We are not surprised that numbers remain solid even amid the recent C-suite turmoil (nothing has had any time to change). On the positive, the company appears wedded to their current trajectory around supply commitments and seems to continue to desire supporting the ecosystem (though some of the commentary around backstops and investments does sound slightly more measured). ... On the other hand however it does sound like hope for a Jensen return may be somewhat futile (they were clear that the current Board does not want him back) and hence the broader investor concerns around what the company might look like in the longer term ex-Jensen remain (for example concerns over new supplier negotiations, roadmap setting, speed of action, and employee retention as well as headline risk around new potential investigations)."

Barclays: Overweight, $210

"The company answered the two most important questions on investors' minds 1) does Jensen's departure mean a change in the revenue forecast, and 2) is there a way for him back into the company. To the first point, the raise of FY28 growth to +75% Y/Y (vs. prior +70% Y/Y) shows that at least in the near-term this wasn't a shell game with China soaking up excess demand (like many had called out over the past week). However, the company didn't go so far as to explicitly comment on China's indirect access through SE Asia and that will remain an overhang into CY27."

Truist: Hold, $174

"Management says 'We got this,' but it's just not that easy. NVDA delivered solid Q3 results and Q4 guidance (ex-margins), and raised its CY27 sales growth outlook from +70% to +75%. Unfortunately, the most challenging questions were not asked on the call. Specifically: (1) How much revenue might new Dept of Commerce rules curtail? (2) What will be the effect of the political power shift in the U.S. on land/power/shell availability in the coming 1-2 years? and (3) What's the status of the CEO direct report engagement?"

Jefferies: Buy, $250

The bank lowered its target from $300.

"There are few buyers in this market for AI-related names, but hard not to be constructive with such strong demand vs such a low valuation. Management noted that cloud industry backlog reached $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion three months ago, while Hopper GPUs have recontracted at up to twice their original price and B300 rental rates have increased more than 60% since introduction. In our view, higher rental rates across GPU generations provide tangible evidence that available supply remains well below demand."

JPMorgan: Overweight, $230

The bank hiked its price target from $215.

"We think there's a strong case to be made that shares will remain highly volatile in the near-term. Nonetheless, on the back of tonight's results and management's stronger near-to-mid-term outlook, we are raising our estimates."

Wells Fargo: Overweight, $250

Wells Fargo trimmed its price target from $300.

"NVDA delivered solid results / guide & more importantly raised F28 rev guide to +75% y/y off higher base. While NT headline risks could persist, we remain positive on NVDA's portfolio breadth + supply chain execution."

Citi: Buy, $225

"Nvidia earnings reinforced our core investment thesis that demand remains very strong, supply constraints are easing, and interim management is confident enough to raise long-term growth expectations. Notably, Nvidia's more selective approach to financing AI infrastructure projects could moderate growth for some neocloud operators if funding becomes constrained."

TD Cowen: Buy, $200

"Despite the turmoil, messaging was business as usual. F2028 guidance increased to +75% off a higher base, with consistent GM% comments as Rubin ramps. Demand still > supply but C2028 is the investor debate. Tonight addressed some immediate concerns, but lots of outstanding questions."

UBS: Buy, $220

The bank lowered its price target from $240.

"One could read the C2027 commentary and additional purchase commits as somewhat of a relief for the supply chain, but there was not much added for C2028, so questions about the impact from a slowdown are likely to persist."

data.title: U.S. oil price slides as data shows larger-than-expected increases in crude, gasoline stocks
data.description:
Crude oil futures fell Wednesday as the market continued to focus more on strong supply than on the conflict in the Middle East.

Oil was part of a broad retreat across commodities as the dollar strengthened to a fresh 19-month high, creating a headwind for raw materials priced in the currency.

The Brent crude benchmark has retreated by more than 20% so far this month, as supplies from the Middle East recovered and President Trump held off on renewed large-scale strikes against Iran, although low-level fighting has flared up across the region recently.

While recovering Middle East supply keeps crude under pressure, continued attacks on vessels around the Strait of Hormuz and renewed strikes on Persian Gulf infrastructure "highlight the fragility of this recovery," Sparta Commodities oil analyst Abhishek Kumar said in a note.

Russian refining is still disrupted by Ukrainian attacks, with crude exports rising as refinery outages limit domestic processing, developments that "continue to support a geopolitical premium in European diesel despite the broader weakness in crude," Kumar added.

The decline in U.S. crude futures was exacerbated by the U.S. Energy Information Administration's weekly report showing larger-than-expected increases in crude oil and gasoline inventories, adding to expectations of a supply surplus.

U.S. commercial crude oil stocks excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve rose by 3.4M barrels to 417.8M in the week ended November 13 and were 3% below the five-year average for the time of year, according to the EIA.

U.S. gasoline inventories increased by 5.2M barrels to 215.9M barrels and were 3% above the five-year average for the time of year, and distillate fuel stocks rose by 1.6M barrels to 104.9M barrels and were 7% below the five-year average for the time of year, the EIA said.

The stock builds added to selling pressure, Gelber & Associates analysts said, adding, "Attacks involving Iran and commercial shipping ​still threaten deliveries through the Strait of Hormuz, but those risks have provided limited support against the growing expectation of a global surplus."

On Wednesday, front-month Nymex crude for December delivery fell 3.2% to $83.26/bbl, its lowest settlement value since August 26, and front-month Brent crude for January delivery slipped 1.3% to $91.95/bbl, its lowest close since November 10.

Additionally, front-month Nymex December natural gas rose 5.1% to $3.372/MMBtu, its best settlement value since February 6, as cooler weather forecasts improved the near-term demand outlook.

data.title: Musk says he felt 'pretty foolish' about scale of midterm spending after Republican rout
data.description:
By Harshita Mary Varghese and Shivansh Tiwary

Elon Musk said on Wednesday he felt "pretty foolish" about the amount of money he spent on this year's US midterm elections after Republicans suffered sweeping losses.

The CEO of Tesla and SpaceX , and the world's richest man, spent nearly half a billion dollars to back Republican candidates and keep Texas red — a state home to his automaker Tesla, rocket-to-AI company SpaceX and a planned chipmaking venture between the two.

Those election-spending bets unraveled as Democrats seized both chambers of Congress, and Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican Greg Abbott in the Texas governor's race, in a stinging rebuke to US President Donald Trump, a close Musk ally whom the billionaire helped elect.

"I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it," Musk said, speaking virtually at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday.

He added it was possible Republican candidates would have fared worse without the spending, but said the result demonstrated that campaign cash alone could not determine an election.

"Probably, if I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money," he said.

Turning to his own AI ambitions, Musk said Anthropic was "extremely likely" to continue renting computing capacity from SpaceX and wanted significantly more.

He said the highest-probability outcome was for Anthropic to seek an additional 10 gigawatts of computing capacity from SpaceX.
